title: Tenses Quiz 1
description: Choose between the two present tenses and build the forms correctly.
instructions: Tenses: Present simple and present continuous.
Read each question carefully, then check your answer.
Every question has a trap. Read every word.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
options: She working in a bank every day.
She works in a bank every day.
She are work in a bank every day.
She work in a bank every day.
questions.explanation: With she, the present simple adds -s. Watch out: the continuous needs am, is or are plus -ing, never the bare -ing alone.

questions.question: Which question is correct?
options: Is he play football on Sundays?
Does he plays football on Sundays?
Does he play football on Sundays?
Do he play football on Sundays?
questions.explanation: After does, the verb stays in the base form. Watch out: the -s is already carried by does, so it cannot be added again.

questions.question: My brother {{1}} (watch) television every evening.
questions.explanation: Verbs ending in -ch add -es in the present simple. Watch out: not watchs.

questions.question: Look! The children {{1}} (play) in the garden.
questions.explanation: Look! signals something happening now, so the present continuous is needed: are + playing.

questions.question: 'I am knowing the answer' is correct English.
questions.explanation: Know is a verb of state, so we say I know the answer. Watch out: verbs of state (know, like, want, believe) are not used in the continuous.

questions.question: Which sentence is correct?
questions.explanation: Believe is a verb of state and takes the simple form. Watch out: with I, there is no -s.

questions.question: Complete the table with the correct forms.
questions.explanation: The present simple adds -s (-es after o) for he, she, it; the continuous is am / is / are + -ing. Watch out: go becomes goes, not gos.

questions.question: Match each sentence with its use.
left: The sun rises in the east.
I am reading a good book these days.
right: a fact that is always true
questions.explanation: Each tense matches a different idea. Watch out: the present simple can describe the future when it is a timetable.

questions.question: Put the words in the correct order.
questions.explanation: The negative of the present simple is subject + does not + base verb.

questions.question: Which time words usually go with the present simple?
questions.explanation: Frequency words fit the present simple; at the moment and right now fit the present continuous. Watch out: today can fit both, so read the whole sentence.

questions.question: What is the -ing form of 'run'?
questions.explanation: After one short vowel and a consonant, the last consonant is doubled. Watch out: sit, sitting and swim, swimming follow the same rule.

questions.question: Correct the mistake: She don't like tea.
questions.explanation: With she, the helping verb is does, not do. Watch out: negative sentences keep the main verb in the base form.
